correctness.rationale: For odd characteristic not three, depressed cubic coordinates (s,A,B) are unique. Since u≠0, the shear (s,B)↦(B,B+v−us) is bijective. For A≠0, the discriminant character sum and rational root multiplicity census imply exactly (q−chi_q(−3))/3 root-free cubic constant terms. At A=0 the cube map supplies the two regimes. Exactly two A-values touch zero, giving the printed formula. All hypotheses, double-root cases, and extremal q=5 are accounted for. A standalone root-by-root verifier independently checks 84 shifts in eight fields, including extensions, without substituting experiments for proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected archival 2012 work gives only large-q asymptotics for polynomial differences. The strongest inspected 2017 exact paper treats scalar shifts and does not imply a result on degree-one polynomial differences; an affine variable change cannot lower difference degree. Existing squarefreeness correlation work counts a broader, differently partitioned set and does not determine irreducible pairs. Dedicated published-finding corpus and literature searches found no exact equivalent; the inaccessible historical 2002 chapter is explicitly disclosed as a real risk.
residual_risks: The full text of the 2002 Effinger--Hicks--Mullen chapter was unavailable and might contain equivalent exact results; only its abstract was read.
The full original 2009 Bender--Pollack proof was not inspected, although the subsequent 2012 source explicitly identifies its results as asymptotic.
A general unlocated identity for correlations of depressed cubic irreducibility or nonconstant polynomial shifts could subsume the theorem.
Semantic database retrieval is incomplete and does not establish global priority.

value.rationale: Gives an exact closed count, unconditional existence and full u,v-uniformity for a natural class of function-field twin primes for all odd finite fields of characteristic other than three. This is a genuine exact strengthening of archival asymptotic counts on this structural subfamily and sharply contrasts with elliptic-curve corrections for constant shifts. The full-field and all-shifts classification with mod-three arithmetic split is substantive; it is not an arbitrary small cutoff or a recomputation of published tables.
